endorsements.quote: For the same reason, attention should be paid to any updates made to the algorithms and validation of their performance before widespread adoption in a radiology practice.

unlisted_practices: Expand the number and availability of extensive and unbiased training sets for AI development.
Vendors and researchers should develop improved techniques to mitigate the brittleness of algorithms.
Professional organizations, interest groups, and regulatory agencies should develop standards around good machine learning practices and clarify algorithm validation pathways.
Do not treat analytic (technical) validation alone as evidence of clinical validation of imaging AI tools.
Develop standardized templates for data sharing agreements.
Use federated or distributed learning to build diverse training datasets without centralizing patient data.
Monitor the performance of clinically deployed AI algorithms through a registry.
Address barriers to equitable access to advanced imaging, particularly for underserved and rural populations.

screen.reason: This is a strategic plan and commentary paper from the American Cancer Society National Lung Cancer Roundtable outlining priorities and challenges for implementation of advanced imaging and AI across the lung cancer continuum.
